title: Differentiable JPEG-based Input Perturbation for Knowledge Distillation Amplification via Conditional Mutual Information Maximization
claim: Plug-in perturbation layer before a frozen model is trained, then reused in distillation, with its internals shown.
layout: 3 panels: two stages on top, JPEG layer detail below, left-to-right
description: The figure has three parts. The top row has two gray rounded panels, Training Stage on the left and Distillation Stage on the right. In training, a Raw Image x goes into an orange Differentiable JPEG Layer inside a blue Coded Teacher box. The compressed image x̃_w then feeds a gray trapezoid network f_θt, which produces a loss box (L_CE minus λL_DJIP). In distillation, the raw image goes to both a student network f_θs and the coded teacher, and both outputs feed a combined L_KD loss box. The bottom panel expands the orange Differentiable JPEG Layer. A bird photo x passes through RGB-to-YCbCr conversion with blockwise DCT, then a differentiable soft quantizer Q_d, then YCbCr-to-RGB conversion with blockwise IDCT. This yields a slightly blocky compressed bird image x̃_w. An equation below the stages gives x̃_w = J_d(x; w) = J_d(x; Q, α), with the trainable parameters in red.
caption: The overall training framework of DJIP is shown, centered around a differentiable JPEG coded teacher module (blue), which integrates a differentiable JPEG layer (orange). The process involves two stages: differentiable JPEG layer training and student distillation, with trainable parameters highlighted in red.
abstract: Maximizing conditional mutual information (CMI) has recently been shown to enhance the effectiveness of teacher networks in knowledge distillation (KD). Prior work achieves this by fine-tuning a pretrained teacher to maximize a proxy of its CMI. However, fine-tuning large-scale teachers is often impractical, and proxy-based optimization introduces inaccuracies. To overcome these limitations, we propose Differentiable JPEG-based Input Perturbation (DJIP), a plug-and-play framework that improves teacher–student knowledge transfer without modifying the teacher. DJIP employs a trainable differentiable JPEG layer inserted before the teacher to perturb teacher inputs in a way that directly increases CMI. We further introduce a novel alternating optimization algorithm to efficiently learn the coding parameters of the JPEG layer to maximize the perturbed CMI. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, across diverse distillers and architectures, demonstrate that DJIP consistently improves student accuracy-achieving up to 4.11% gains-while remaining computationally lightweight and fully compatible with standard KD pipelines.
